chunk_findings.detail: The stamp-only step runs *after* `_close`, which is the function whose own docstring says it "end[s] the run's record: the upgrade itself when something was settled, else a failure." In exactly the case `_stamp_only` was added for — no results this run because every item is already acknowledged (so `ok` is empty) and the plan no longer lists anything — `_close` takes the `elif run:` branch and appends `run failed: "upgrade <frm> -> <to>: nothing settled"`. Only then does `_stamp_only` append a second, contradicting event `upgrade.applied {from: frm, to: to, target: to, categories: cats, items: []}`. Reproduce: project stamped 0.1.11 with 0.2.1 installed, all 0.2.1 items settled, run `ddflow upgrade --apply`; the committed log receives, for the same `run` id, a failed note followed by an applied event that advances the release to 0.2.1. Two problems follow from the ordering: (1) the run is recorded as failed even though the stamp was advanced, so any tooling/operator surface that resolves a run's outcome from `_close`'s note (the reason the `status: "done"`/`run` fields exist) reports the upgrade as unsuccessful; (2) the applied event is written with `run=""` (the call passes `""` for `run`), so it carries no `run`/`status` fields and cannot be attributed to the run that produced it. The stamp-only record should be written from inside/`_close`'s success path (or `_close`'s failure branch skipped when `_stamp_only` will advance), so a run is not simultaneously "failed" and "applied".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply.py:_stamp_only (call site after `_close`)

chunk_findings.detail: `settled_items` only credits a partial apply when the release it recorded as `target` is equal to the *current* `running` version. But `running` is the code version installed at the time `upgrade --plan` is executed, and a partial apply records whatever version was heading it at apply time (the diff's own comment says so: "an apply that recorded the release it headed for counts only when that is the running one"). Whenever the tool is upgraded between the partial apply and the next plan — exactly the environment described in the bug (project stamp 0.1.11, 0.2.1 installed) — the recorded target no longer equals `running`, so the record's acknowledged items are not added to `settled`, `config_items(changes, cfg)` re-emits them (changes for 0.2.0 are still `_wanted` because 0.2.0 <= running 0.2.1 and > baseline 0.1.11), and the plan is non-empty again. Concrete sequence: project stamp 0.1.11, ddflow 0.2.0 installed; `upgrade --apply` acknowledges the 0.2.0 config items, one item refused so the stamp stays 0.1.11, the record is written with `target="0.2.0"`, `from="0.1.11"`, `to="0.1.11"`; operator installs ddflow 0.2.1; `upgrade --plan` now calls `settled_items` with `running="0.2.1"`, the guard rejects the record because `"0.2.0" != "0.2.1"`, the acknowledged 0.2.0 items reappear in the plan, and the next `--apply` re-acknowledges them and appends another full batch to the committed event log — the "plan never empties / log grows every run" bug this change is supposed to fix. The id sets are the same config-item ids (config item ids are derived from the same `config_items` call), so filtering them by id would have been safe here; the target check is the only thing keeping them in the plan.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_plan.py:settled_items (the `if u.get("target") in (None, "", running):` guard, ~line 95)

chunk_findings.detail: `_stamp_only` is invoked *after* `_close`, and it fires in exactly the case the change is meant to handle: the plan is already fully acknowledged (`_unresolved(plan, set())` is false), `results` is empty, and the stamp still lags (`frm != to`). In that case `run_nemo_run` has already called `_close(log, run, selected, ok, (frm, new_to, to), ...)` with `ok` empty (nothing was settled this run), so `_close` takes its `elif run:` branch and appends `_note(log, run, "failed", summary="upgrade <frm> -> <to>: nothing settled")` before `_stamp_only` appends the successful `upgrade.applied` event and returns `to`. Concrete input: a project that just had a partial apply (all 63 items acknowledged, stamp still `0.1.11`) is run through `ddflow upgrade --apply` against `0.2.1`; the run now advances the stamp, but every such run — and every later idempotent re-run where `frm == to` and `_stamp_only` returns early — still appends an `upgrade.run failed: nothing settled` note, because `_close` is reached with an empty `ok` regardless. So the run is logged as failed while the upgrade succeeded, and the log keeps growing by one failed note per `--apply`, which is the very non-idempotency/status problem the change set out to remove; the stamp-only handling needs to be folded into `_close` (or `_close` must be made aware that a stamp-only advance counts as success) so no failure note accompanies the stamp advance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply.py:_stamp_only (with _close)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_stamp_only` provably cannot change the version the run reports, and its only observable effect is a second `_record` call for the same run. Walk the guard: it acts only when `not results and frm != to and not _unresolved(plan, set())`. The unchanged line immediately above it, `new_to = (frm or UNSTAMPED) if _unresolved(plan, ok) else to`, calls the same predicate on the same `plan` with `ok` (a superset of the empty ack set used by `_stamp_only`; when `results` is empty `ok` is empty too). If no item is unresolved with *no* acks, none is unresolved with `ok` either, so by the time `_stamp_only` runs, `new_to` is already `to` — the function returns `to`, i.e. exactly its input. In the other branch it returns its input verbatim. So `new_to = _stamp_only(...)` is a no-op assignment in every case, and the function's sole behaviour is the additional `_record(log, [], set(), frm, to, cats, backup_dir, reasons)`.

Concrete case: a project that was partially applied earlier (say the refused item was dropped and the rest were settled) so the now-filtered plan is empty while the stamp still lags — `frm="0.1.11"`, `to="0.2.1"`, `results=[]`. Line 341 sets `new_to="0.2.1"` and `_close(...)` (same `log`/`cats`/`backup_dir`/`reasons` parameter list as `_record`) records the `0.1.11 → 0.2.1` upgrade; `_stamp_only` then fires and calls `_record` a second time for the identical transition, so `ddflow upgrade --apply` still appends a duplicate upgrade event to the committed log on that invocation rather than being a no-op — the append-per-run behaviour the bug report complains about (log growing without new work) — and `settled_items` must then tolerate two stamp-moving events for one run. The docstring's claim that this function "moves the project to the release when the stamp still lags" is not met; the stamp move comes entirely from the pre-existing `_close` line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply.py `_stamp_only` (called at the `new_to = _stamp_only(...)` line)
